name: security-jws-detached-payload-review
intent: Detached JWS payload bytes and signature-to-consumer agreement
artifacts: JWS serialization, b64/critical-header handling, HTTP/body transformations and final consumer bytes.
trace: Determine which exact bytes are authenticated and whether normalization/decoding makes the application act on different content than was verified.
experiment: Use local synthetic signed messages and harmless paired payloads differing at one transformation boundary; record verifier and consumer digests.
disproof: A valid signature on an unchanged intended payload is expected; a serialization rejection is not message substitution.
repair: Bind verification to the exact consumed representation and supported header policy, preserving legitimate detached payloads.
branch_decisions: Separate ordinary detached JWS from unencoded-payload b64=false; the latter requires correct b64/crit processing. Signature validity and identical byte digests do not ensure equivalent JSON meaning if duplicate members have first/last parser differences. Bind accepted algorithm/key and parse the verified bytes consistently, rejecting ambiguous structures where the application contract requires uniqueness.
